video.title: AI Told Me to Start This Business. So I Did.

summary: Chris Koerner demonstrates how he validates an online business idea before launching, using the example of a cheap, AI-enabled QuickBooks/Xero competitor for businesses with 0-10 employees. He runs the same research prompt through Perplexity Labs, Manus, Claude Opus 4.1 and ChatGPT-5 agent mode, mines Reddit complaints with GummySearch, and explains paid polling with PickFu ($1 per response). The research converges on unreliable bank feeds, rising and unpredictable pricing and poor support as the top pain points, suggesting a 'cheap price forever, never breaks' positioning. He then builds a landing page on Carrd connected to a Namecheap domain and Beehiiv in eight minutes, and announces LazyBooks at $19/month, built for 0-10 employee businesses.

tactics.name: Multi-AI market validation
steps: Write one specific research prompt naming review sources (Capterra, G2, Software Advice, TrustRadius) and asking for top 10 pain points, must-have features, opportunity map and viability
Run it in parallel in Perplexity Labs, Manus agent, Claude with deep research, and ChatGPT agent mode
Answer clarifying questions on target segment and differentiation
Compare outputs; apply the 80/20 rule to focus on the top two complaints

quote.text: these AI tools are only as good as the prompts I give them, and they're only as good as the places I tell them to go and extract data from
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Reddit complaint mining with GummySearch
steps: Buy a $10 day pass
Create an audience of relevant subreddits (about 10M members)
Search the competitor name and use Patterns to summarise 100 submissions
Compare sentiment scores across competitors
Use Ask to find the most common complaint; turn its opposite into the marketing message
Track topics for email alerts

tactics.name: Paid polling without an audience
steps: Create a PickFu poll with a targeted question
Choose 100 respondents filtered to the target (e.g. US small business owners)
Pay about $1 per response; results within an hour
More targeting costs more

tactics.name: 8-minute waitlist landing page
steps: Duplicate an existing Carrd landing page
Add headline and email field
Connect a custom domain via Namecheap A and CNAME records
Connect Beehiiv via API key and publication ID
Collect UTM parameters to segment signups
Publish and test with a plus-addressed email

quote.text: I'm going to show you how I personally launch landing pages that can start collecting emails in about 3 to four minutes
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Search Facebook groups and Reddit manually
steps: Search moderated small-business Facebook groups and niche subreddits for competitor names
Paste open post URLs into ChatGPT to summarise

warnings.warning: Accounting software is crowded and mature; customer acquisition will be expensive and bank integrations are complex.

quote.text: Says customer acquisition will be expensive. Bank integration complexity is significant. Feature creep pressure is inevitable
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

warnings.warning: ChatGPT-5 won't use agentic features unless explicitly asked.
Highly targeted PickFu polls cost more.

lessons.lesson: Validate demand cheaply before building: mine complaints, poll strangers and put up a waitlist.
Turn competitors' top complaint into your headline (e.g. 'cheap price forever' against rising prices).
A commodity market is a massive market; you can win by executing basics properly rather than disrupting.
Complaint lists follow 80/20: focus on the top two pain points.
Serve a neglected segment (0-10 employee businesses) that incumbents serve poorly by trying to serve everyone.

quote.text: both market leaders suffer from serving everyone and therefore they are serving small businesses with 0 to 10 employees poorly
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: Specific prompts that name sources get better AI research output.
Without an audience you can rent one through paid polling panels.

evidence_quality.rationale: Live research demo of an unlaunched idea; no revenue or traction data; AI-generated summaries are second-hand.
evidence_quality.promotional_conflict: Promotes LazyBooks and tkowners.com; affiliate links for some tools.
